sections.title: Freshman Discovery Project
sections.description: This course is meant to be fun and exciting! Students will create a real project of their choosing that will help them to gain excitement about continuing in one of the computing majors. This is a 2-credit course designed to provide freshman students in Computing Degrees at BYU-Idaho with the opportunity to engage in hands-on project development. This course is intended to be taken during the second semester of the freshman year. Students enrolled in CSE199R should have completed or be enrolled concurrently in CSE 111 Programming with Functions or have equivalent programming experience. Students will have the freedom to choose and develop a project of their own interest, leveraging the skills and knowledge acquired from previous coursework or personal exploration. The course emphasizes self-directed learning and project management, as students will not be provided with formal learning materials or structured assignments. Instead, they will have the autonomy to define their project scope, set milestones, and implement solutions using appropriate technologies and methodologies.

sections.title: Product Development Project
sections.description: This course is meant to be fun and exciting! Students will create a real project of their choosing that will help them to gain excitement about continuing in one of the computing majors. This is a 2-credit course designed to provide junior students in Computing Degrees at BYU-Idaho with the opportunity to engage in hands-on project development to complete a real product. This course is intended to be taken during the junior year, any time after completing CSE 310. Students will have the freedom to choose and develop a project of their own interest, leveraging the skills and knowledge acquired from previous coursework or personal exploration. The course emphasizes self-directed learning to create a real-world product. Students will not be provided with formal learning materials or structured assignments. Instead, they will have the autonomy to define their project scope, set milestones, and implement solutions using appropriate technologies and methodologies.

sections.title: Math for the Real World
sections.description: Prepares students to understand, analyze, and solve real-life problems that require quantitative reasoning. Topics include the meaning of probabilities; how to read, critique, and apply statistical information found in news reports, public policy debates, consumer reports, and other daily life and professional situations; the use of mathematical models in describing, understanding, and making predictions about real-world phenomena; and the mathematics of budgeting, loans, and investments. Examples and applications from daily life and natural phenomena will illustrate topics. Inspires students to act wisely when faced with quantitative challenges in collegiate coursework, employment, and daily living.

sections.title: Applied Calculus: Data Analysis
sections.description: The three topic pillars of this course are functions, derivatives, and integrals. We will work on broadening and deepening our understanding of functions as tools of mathematics and as models. We will focus on a derivative as defined by its role in the local approximation of a curve and use derivatives in optimization. We will focus on integrals as a way to compute probabilities and will explore the connection between the probability density function (pdf) and cumulative distribution function (cdf) for a continuous random variable. We will fit models to data visually, by maximizing log likelihood functions, and by using a method of moments. We will rely on software (R and Mathematica) to help us with our calculations in this course.

sections.title: Tutoring Mathematics
sections.description: This course gives math education majors an early practicum experience working with secondary-level students. We hope that participants will discover whether or not they really want to pursue a secondary education degree. During this practicum experience, participants will tutor secondary students, discuss and use "best" practices in tutoring, improve their presentation skills, and prepare for the Praxis Exam requirement. Students will visit local schools for 2 hours each week between the hours of 8:30 am and 3:30 pm outside of the weekly class meeting. Travel time and school schedules need to be considered in the students' planning for these visits. Students are responsible for arranging their transportation.

sections.description: This course focuses on formulating and solving boundary value problems modeling heat flow, wave motion, and electric potential. Methods of solution include separation of variables and eigenfunction expansion, including Fourier series. Techniques are developed for homogeneous problems and extended to problems with nonhomogeneous PDEs or boundary conditions. Topics typically include Sturm-Liouville theory and generalization to higher dimensions and non-Cartesian coordinate systems. Additional topics may include the method of characteristics, transform methods, and quasi- or non-linear equations.

sections.title: Stat & Data Science Consulting
sections.description: This is a hands-on introduction to statistical consulting. Students will apply skills developed in other statistical courses to provide consulting services to researchers at BYU-Idaho. Students will continue to develop the written and oral communication skills needed to discuss technical statistical content with other researchers. Projects address needs at all stages of the research process. Student activity will be closely monitored by a statistician. This course provides a foundation upon which a student with interest in statistics can provide meaningful service and enhance their skills.

sections.title: Sec Ed Math Teaching Methods
sections.description: Math 490 must be taken the semester before student teaching. This course is designed to help pre-service secondary mathematics teachers apply research-based teaching strategies that lead students to discover, create, appreciate, and utilize mathematics. Students will have many opportunities to teach, prepare lesson plans, learn how to organize and manage classrooms, and connect these activities to state and professional standards for secondary mathematics teachers. Students will also practice using the principles of the BYU-Idaho Learning Model in their own teaching.

sections.title: Math Ed Practicum Lab
sections.description: Pre-service teachers will serve as teaching assistants under the direction of a mentor teacher in a public school classroom providing an authentic experience with the responsibilities of a professional educator and an opportunity to practice the teaching skills being learned in their methods class. As teaching assistants, pre-service teachers will work one-on-one or in small groups with select students, help with grading class assessments, aid with record keeping, assist with class activities, create teaching resources, and teach lessons as assigned by the mentor teacher. Students will visit local schools daily during the time scheduled for this class. Additional travel time may need to be considered in the students' planning for these visits. Students are responsible for arranging their transportation.

sections.description: Internship credits are exempt from tuition charges.
